## From a problem to hardware freedom {#motivation-hardware-freedom}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="47%"}
::: {.r-stack .motivation-layer-states}
![](assets/images/motivation/abstraction-layers-step-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="0" fig-alt="Computer-science abstraction layers from problem and algorithm through software, ISA, RTL, circuits, devices, and physical implementation"}
![](assets/images/motivation/abstraction-layers-step-3.svg){.fragment .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="0" fig-alt="Computer-science abstraction layers with arrows crossing the instruction-set boundary from compiler IRs to hardware logic"}

:::

::: {.column width="53%"}
:::: {.r-stack .motivation-layer-copy}
::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .fade-out .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
<div class="motivation-state-label">One intent, many representations</div>

- Each level makes different decisions as the design becomes more physical.

- A conventional compiler targets a **fixed machine and instruction set**.
:::

::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
<div class="motivation-state-label">Cross the ISA boundary</div>

<div class="motivation-impact">
  <span>More specialization</span>
  <span class="motivation-impact-arrow">→</span>
  <span>More opportunities for optimization</span>
</div>

- Choose operators, widths, parallelism, memories, and pipeline stages.

- Specialize or fuse operations, then map them to LUTs, DSPs, or gates
  [@dinechin2024asa].
:::

## Some machines are experts at specialization {#motivation-fp8-gpu}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPU module. [@nvidia2022hopper]](assets/images/motivation/nvidia-h100-sxm5.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPU module with the central Hopper GPU and surrounding HBM stacks" height="250"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![Google's first TPU board and TPUs deployed in a datacenter. [@google2017tpu]](assets/images/motivation/google-tpu-v1.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Google's first Tensor Processing Unit on a circuit board beside racks of deployed TPU servers" height="250"}
:::
::::

::: {.incremental}
- **Pressure:** AI makes matrix multiplication the hot loop.

- **Machines:** Tensor Cores and TPUs put matrix engines on silicon
  [@jouppi2017tpu; @jouppi2020tpu].

- **Arithmetic:** BF16, FP8, and smaller formats trade precision for more
  operations per watt [@micikevicius2022fp8].
:::

## Promotion time! {#motivation-team-arithmetic}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
![*Application-Specific Arithmetic*, de Dinechin and Kumm, 2024. [@dinechin2024asa]](assets/images/motivation/application-specific-arithmetic-cover.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Cover of Application-Specific Arithmetic by Florent de Dinechin and Martin Kumm" height="520"}
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
**Today's bias:** we will look at hardware through **arithmetic** and **small
floating-point formats**.

::: {.incremental}
- **Emeraude:** make number formats and operators part of the design space
  [@uguen2020hls; @dinechin2024asa].

- **FloPoCo:** generate arithmetic operators for a target, a frequency, and a
  numerical contract.

- **Hands-on:** build an E4M3 multiplier; if time permits, specialize it into a
  squarer.
:::
:::
::::
